option_relations.rationale: Acute coronary syndrome (non-ST-elevation or ST-elevation myocardial infarction) is a distinct cardiac condition caused by plaque rupture or thrombosis, not directly related to myocardial metastasis.

ST-segment elevation due to myocardial metastasis from squamous cell carcinoma of the lung describes a specific manifestation (ST-elevation) and etiology (squamous cell carcinoma metastasis) of myocardial metastasis.
Cardiac metastasis from lung cancer (intracardiac mass) is clinically equivalent to Myocardial Metastasis, as the mass is located within the myocardium.
Metastatic cardiac tumor (secondary to lung cancer) is clinically equivalent to Myocardial Metastasis, as it describes a tumor in the heart that originated from lung cancer.
